one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Tiruppur-based designer, engineer, manufacturer and exporter of performance and technical garments for institutional, government and brand clients in international markets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company is engaged in the design, engineering, manufacture and export of performance garments for institutional, government and brand clients in international markets, having begun operations as a partnership firm in 1994 and been incorporated as a company in 2006. Its portfolio spans military uniforms, tactical outerwear, high-visibility workwear, weather-resistant and all-weather outerwear, police and border patrol uniforms, protective workwear and performance activewear. Garments are produced to client specifications and compliance requirements of European military, government and institutional buyers, with clients across Europe (including Switzerland) and North America (including the United States).

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: In-house manufacturing with no outsourcing of production. All key manufacturing processes for engineered garment manufacturing are available in-house, including seam sealing, bonded and stitch-free assembly, laser cutting, ultrasonic welding, reflective fusing, quilting and down filling; the DRHP states that keeping these processes under one roof allows better control of quality, production time and cost. The manufacturing process runs Material Inward, Fabric and Accessory Checking, Fabric Cutting, Sewing and Technical Assembly, Ironing, Checking/Finishing and Final Packing, with quality-control checkpoints at each stage. Upstream, the Company is not backward integrated into fabric: raw materials are primarily sourced from third-party suppliers in international and local markets - fabric development is carried out through external suppliers, and waterproof membranes, seam-sealing tapes, coatings, reflective materials, waterproof zippers and yarns are sourced from suppliers in Europe, the Far East and other markets. Imported purchases were 73.80% of total purchases for the period ended September 30, 2025, 71.47% in Fiscal 2025, 63.89% in Fiscal 2024 and 69.38% in Fiscal 2023 (Rs.1,123.45 / 2,581.21 / 1,130.33 / 1,220.18 lakhs), with domestic purchases at 26.20%, 28.53%, 36.11% and 30.62% (Rs.398.74 / 1,030.25 / 638.81 / 538.61 lakhs) respectively. Inbound materials move by sea for planned orders with longer lead times and by air for sampling and urgent programmes; outbound finished garments are exported by sea for regular production shipments and by air for express and seasonal deliveries, with stated proximity to Tuticorin port and Chennai sea port and airport. Power is met through the Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited and solar power panels installed at the factory; water is met through the Tiruppur City Municipal Corporation. The Company states it has no collaborations, tie-ups or joint ventures and no export obligation as on the date of the DRHP.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue is predominantly export-derived - exports accounted for 99.83% of revenue from operations for the period ended September 30, 2025, 93.87% in FY2025, 87.77% in FY2024 and 94.99% in FY2023
- Geographic mix skewed to Switzerland (74.88% of revenue for the period 01/04/2025 to 30/09/2025 versus 58.87% in FY2024-25), with the USA share declining from 32.71% in FY2024-25 to 23.13%
- Product mix weighted to woven garments (61.70% of revenue for the period ended September 30, 2025 and 72.39% in FY2024-25), with knitted at 38.30% and 27.61% respectively
- Existing production capacity is operating at near-optimal utilisation levels, with growth dependent on the planned additional facility
- In-house manufacturing of specialized processes is stated to streamline inventory management and production, minimize production time and bring cost effectiveness
- Cost control approach based on measuring and benchmarking costs at each cost center against industry/scientific standards to control direct costs and overheads
- Fabrics and accessories are sourced through external suppliers, including global suppliers of technical materials such as seam-sealing tapes, reflective materials, waterproof zippers and specialized coatings
- Customer base is highly concentrated - top 10 customers accounted for 100% of sales (excluding other operating revenue) for the period ended September 30, 2025 and 99.70% in FY2025

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Continue to invest in technological capabilities, including establishing an additional manufacturing facility in Tiruppur dedicated to complex outerwear and high-performance products, as existing capacity is operating at near-optimal utilisation
- Focus on premium international brands - build relationships with outdoor and performance wear brands in Europe and North America, approaching select brands to offer production capacity, showcase the facility and certifications and provide samples demonstrating seam-sealed, bonded and laminated construction capability
- Focus on consistently meeting quality standards - continue investing in quality control infrastructure including testing equipment and trained personnel to maintain consistency of output as volumes increase with the planned capacity expansion
- Maintain cordial relationships with suppliers, customers and employees - regular engagement with global suppliers of technical materials (seam-sealing tapes, reflective materials, waterproof zippers, specialized coatings) and investment in workforce training on seam-sealing machines, ultrasonic welders and laser cutters
- Continue to strive for cost efficiency - measuring and benchmarking costs at each cost center to industry/scientific standards to control direct costs and overheads, maintaining cost discipline while increasing output at the new facility

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Existing production capacity at the Tiruppur facility (installed capacity 450,000 garment pieces per annum, built-up area over 45,000 square feet) is stated to be operating at near-optimal utilisation levels. To support future growth and increasing demand from premium international outdoor and performance wear brands, the Company plans to establish an additional manufacturing facility spread over approximately 1.41 acres in Tiruppur, dedicated to complex outerwear and high-performance products. The proposed facility is expected to enhance technical capabilities, increase production capacity and improve operational efficiencies, enabling larger and more value-added programs while maintaining quality and compliance standards, and is expected to strengthen the Company's position in the premium segment, provide greater production flexibility, reduce lead times and generate economies of scale. It is the primary object of the Fresh Issue, with Rs. 3,135.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds earmarked towards the capital expenditure requirement.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- In-house manufacturing facility with quality control mechanism - ISO 9001:2015, 14001:2015 and 45001:2018 certified manufacturer and exporter of knitted and woven garments, with washing/rubbing fastness, shrinkage, seam leakage and button pull testing and final inspections to customer specifications; in-house operations streamline inventory management and production, minimize production time and support cost effectiveness
- Widespread reach in international markets - presence built across Switzerland, USA, UK and India, with international markets the primary area of operation
- Integrated expertise in high performance technical garments - over 20 years producing uniforms and outerwear for the Government of Switzerland (military, Police and other national agencies), with all key engineered-garment processes in-house: seam sealing, bonded and stitch-free assembly, laser cutting, ultrasonic welding, reflective fusing, quilting and down filling under one roof
- Qualified and experienced management team - first- and second-generation entrepreneur Promoters with over 30 years and more than 15 years of experience respectively in the garment export and technical garment segments

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Product concentration in woven garments — Woven garments contributed 61.70% of revenue from product sales for the six-month period ended September 30, 2025 (Rs. 2,366.45 lakhs) and 72.39% in Fiscal 2025 (Rs. 3,823.39 lakhs); any decline from competition, pricing pressure or demand/supply fluctuation would adversely affect results
- Customer concentration — The top customer contributed 41.02% of sales as of September 30, 2025 and approximately 51.51%, 38.13% and 42.01% in Fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023; top 10 customers accounted for 100%, 99.70%, 99.21% and 99.13% of sales in the same periods, and customers often undertake vendor rationalisation
- Geographic / country concentration in Switzerland — Switzerland accounted for 74.88% of revenue for the period 01/04/2025 to 30/09/2025 and 58.87% in FY2024-25, with supply largely to various departments of the Government of Switzerland
- Dependence on exports — Exports accounted for 99.83% of revenue from operations for the period ended September 30, 2025, 93.87% in FY2025, 87.77% in FY2024 and 94.99% in FY2023, concentrating exposure to European and North American demand and cross-border trade conditions
- Single manufacturing location — All manufacturing operations are presently carried out at one facility in Tiruppur, Tamil Nadu, with an installed capacity of 450,000 garment pieces per annum
- Capacity constraint pending the proposed expansion — Existing production capacity is stated to be operating at near-optimal utilisation levels; incremental growth depends on commissioning the proposed additional facility of approximately 1.41 acres at Tiruppur
- Historically weak equity base — Net worth was negative at Rs. (231.53) lakhs in FY2022-23, and RoE for that year was disclosed as not meaningful because average shareholders' equity was negative; net worth has since risen to Rs. 1,382.25 lakhs (FY2024-25) and Rs. 1,931.26 lakhs as of September 30, 2025
- Dependence on external suppliers for raw materials and technical inputs — Raw material sourcing and fabric development are carried out through external suppliers, with global suppliers relied on for seam-sealing tapes, reflective materials, waterproof zippers and specialized coatings
